transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. My name is Dr. Smith — what brings you in to see me today?
I’ve been waking up feeling really heavy and hollow. It’s like the studio lights are on, but there’s no music in me anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way—waking up feeling heavy and hollow?
About nine months now. It’s been there most mornings for that whole time.
Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, even if it felt good at the time?
Yes. There were stretches when I felt dazzlingly alive, but then I’d get suddenly furious if anyone questioned what I was planning or reminded me that my ankle still needed rest.
During those times when you felt 'dazzlingly alive' and irritable, how many days in a row did that usually last?
It started after my ankle injury, and this whole pattern has been going on for about two months now.
Since your ankle injury, have you been taking any pain medications, sedatives, or other substances—prescribed or otherwise—regularly?
I’m not really sure what would count. Could you explain what you mean by “regularly”?
Since your ankle injury, have you taken any pain pills, sedatives, alcohol, or other substances on most days—even if just to help with sleep or pain?
I’m not sure. I mean, I know I took things for the ankle at times, but I couldn’t really say whether it was most days or not.
Can you tell me exactly what medication you were given for your ankle pain—was it an opioid painkiller, a steroid, or something else?
I honestly don’t remember the name of it. I know they gave me something for the pain, but I couldn’t tell you whether it was an opioid or a steroid.
Do you notice these episodes of feeling 'dazzlingly alive' and irritable happening even on days when you haven't taken any pain medication at all?

Yes, there were stretches when I felt dazzlingly alive even apart from the ankle medication. And then if anyone questioned what I was planning, or told me I still needed to rest my ankle, I could get suddenly furious.
